title: Per-address magic-link throttle in own throttles table, keyed by canonical-address HMAC
context: Per-IP limits alone let rotating IPs flood one inbox. Better Auth's rate_limits table prunes rows older than its longest window (60s), so it cannot hold a 10-minute per-address window.
decision: packages/db takeThrottle: fixed-window counter in a throttles table (INSERT ... ON CONFLICT upsert, returns allowed + retryAfterSeconds), windows capped at THROTTLE_MAX_WINDOW_MS (24h), rows older than that pruned by pruneThrottles (1% of calls). Key = 'magic-link:' + HMAC-SHA256(k, canonicalEmail(email)) where k = HMAC-SHA256(AUTH_SECRET, 'wishscene/magic-link-throttle/v1'). canonicalEmail lowercases, strips +tag, and for gmail/googlemail strips dots and maps to gmail.com. 3 links per mailbox per 10 minutes; 429 carries Retry-After.
consequences: Best effort: other alias schemes (Yahoo -tag, catch-all domains) still get one budget per spelling.
A throttled request still leaves an unused verification row that expires in 10 minutes.
alternatives_rejected: Better Auth rate_limits storage: pruned after 60s, window cannot exceed its longest rule.
Keying on the raw normalized address or on a plain hash: stores personal data or a cheaply reversible value.
Keying the HMAC directly with AUTH_SECRET: that secret also signs cookies; purpose-bound derived key instead.
Global per-instance send cap: an attacker could exhaust it for everyone.
